items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is split by family (gray.zig, yuv_rgb.zig, rgb_yuv.zig, scale.zig, yuv_yuv.zig). But the dev work used single-letter names (y, u, v, R) and bare constants (9539, 13075, 6660, 3209), likely carried into the kernels with little documentation of their FFmpeg origins.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: rgb_yuv.zig and yuv_rgb.zig are about 22KB each, probably over 500 lines, which caps this at accept. Fixes were added per conversion (e.g. 444p uses a separate arithmetic path from the table path), suggesting duplicated logic. Late patches to main.zig look ad hoc.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Many magic fixed-point constants (9539, 13075, 76309, 19595/38469/7472). Final perf-check: 'output differs on 3' benchmark workloads, so outputs are silently wrong and the hidden test fails correctness. Input validation is not shown.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Scaled paths are wrong: yuv420p->rgb24 3840x2160->1920x1080 bilinear, rgb24->yuv420p 1920x1080->640x360 and rgb24->rgb24 nearest downscale all DIFFER; s001 only 80 dB. 8 of 58 contract conversions still fail, so general geometry is not handled correctly.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: nm -D lists only swscale_create, swscale_process and swscale_destroy, with no ff_ symbols. build.zig comes from the scaffold, which sets the x86-64-v3 target, and the library builds with plain `zig build`. Single-threaded.
